title: Web / UI design
hint: landing pages, websites, UI, layouts, styling, CSS, visual design
text:
Design with intent, not defaults.
- Pick one clear aesthetic direction (e.g. editorial, minimal-graphite, brutalist, soft-glass) and apply it consistently. Avoid the generic "purple gradient + centered hero + 3 cards" template.
- Typography carries the design: 1–2 families, a real scale (e.g. 14/16/20/28/40/56), tight letter-spacing on large headings, line-height 1.5–1.7 for body, max ~70ch line length.
- Color: define tokens (bg, surface, border, text, muted, accent) as CSS variables; one accent color, used sparingly; check contrast ≥ 4.5:1; provide dark mode via prefers-color-scheme when reasonable.
- Spacing on a 4/8px grid; generous whitespace; align to a grid; consistent radii (pick one: 6, 10 or 14px).
- Hierarchy: one primary action per view; secondary actions visually quieter.
- Real content over lorem ipsum; realistic copy, numbers and states (empty, loading, error, hover, focus-visible, disabled).
- Mobile-first, responsive with fluid widths, no horizontal scroll; touch targets ≥ 40px.
- Subtle motion only (150–250ms ease-out), respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- Semantic HTML, alt text, labels, keyboard navigation.
- Deliver complete, runnable code (single file if not told otherwise), no placeholders like "add more here".

title: Frontend Taste Rules
hint: Frontend UI, landing pages or visual design work
text:
- Build around one idea from the subject's world and show it first, not a generic headline and stats.
- Use one ground, one ink and one accent; the accent marks only the primary action and one other element.
- Never use violet, indigo, cream-and-terracotta palettes, background or text gradients, glassmorphism, neon glows or emoji.
- Keep headlines to two lines; no styled accent words, monospace outside code or tiny tracked uppercase labels.
- Use at most two type families; display at 4-6x body size, body 16-18px, line-height 1.5, 45-75 characters per line.
- Avoid pill badges, 01/02/03 numbering without a real sequence, icon-topped feature cards and rows of identical cards.
- Separate surfaces with tone steps, not hairlines or resting shadows; use one grid with equal 16-32px margins.
- Never invent testimonials, logos or statistics; label placeholders and check 1440, 768 and 390px.

title: Landing Pages and Marketing Sites
hint: Landing pages, marketing sites, product heroes and pricing sections
text:
- Write a hero headline of two lines or fewer that states the product outcome, e.g. 'Ship invoices in 40 seconds', not a category.
- Place one primary CTA above the fold named for its outcome ('Start free trial'), with at most one secondary text link.
- Show the product in the first screen: a real screenshot, a muted loop or a live element covering about half the viewport.
- Order sections by buyer questions: what it does, how it works, proof, pricing, closing CTA; each gets an h2 and a nav anchor.
- Use only real proof with a source; otherwise a clearly marked placeholder, never invented quotes or logo walls.
- Avoid centred heroes over gradient blobs, three identical icon cards and filler words like seamless or revolutionary.
- Keep pricing to two or three tiers; highlight the recommended one with a fill or border, not a glow.

title: App Dashboards and Admin Panels
hint: Dashboards, admin panels, data-dense app screens and settings
text:
- Build the shell first: sidebar 220-260px or 56-64px collapsed, top bar 56-64px, 24px content padding, one scroll container.
- Open each screen with its task: title, one primary action at top right, filters in one row above the content.
- Make tables dense: 36-44px rows, 13-14px text, right-aligned tabular-nums, sticky header, sortable columns.
- Give every panel and table explicit loading, empty and error states; a blank area is never acceptable.
- Use a neutral surface system with low-contrast 1px borders; reserve the accent for selection and primary actions.
- Pair every status colour with a text label; keep semantic hues to success, warning, danger and neutral.
- Edit inline or open details in a 400-480px side drawer instead of page reloads; avoid cards inside cards.

title: Typography and Spacing Systems
hint: Font pairing, type scale, line length and spacing rhythm
text:
- Build UI type on a fixed ratio (1.2 or 1.25) and cap each page at five visible sizes; reserve 4-6x jumps for display headlines.
- Set body text at 16-18px with line-height 1.5-1.6 and headlines at 1.0-1.15 with -0.01 to -0.03em tracking.
- Limit running text to 45-75 characters using max-width in ch units; never let paragraphs span a full 1440px row.
- Build spacing on a 4px base (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96); section gaps should be at least double component gaps.
- Pair fonts by visible contrast, one family with varied weights or two clearly different faces; never a third face.
- Use tabular-nums for prices and table columns, keep text at 12px or above, and align text to one shared left edge.
- Avoid monospace for non-code labels, wide-tracked all-caps captions and centred paragraphs longer than two lines.

title: Color, Tokens and Dark Mode
hint: Color palettes, design tokens, dark mode and theme switching
text:
- Define semantic tokens (background, surface, foreground, muted, border, primary, destructive) as CSS variables; components never use raw hex.
- Build dark mode as its own token set, not an inversion: background near #0E0F12, text at 92-95% lightness, surfaces one step lighter.
- Desaturate accents by 10-20% in dark mode and check each brand colour against both theme backgrounds.
- Honour prefers-color-scheme, persist an explicit choice, and set color-scheme on the root so native controls match.
- Keep one neutral ramp of 9-11 steps, one accent ramp and at most three semantic hues; avoid rainbow palettes and violet defaults.
- Hold body text at 4.5:1 and large text plus UI borders at 3:1; check muted text separately, since it fails most often.
- Avoid gradients on backgrounds and text, coloured glows, and pure #000 backgrounds with pure #FFF text.

title: Charts and Data Visualization
hint: Charts, graphs, data visualization choices, axes and tooltips
text:
- Pick the chart by question: trends use lines, category comparisons use horizontal bars sorted by value, part-of-whole uses at most a donut with three parts.
- Start bar charts at zero, label every axis, and avoid dual y-axes unless the title explains the relationship.
- Use one hue for a single series; cap categorical palettes at six or seven colours and keep series colours consistent across the page.
- Label series directly when there are four or fewer; use a legend only beyond that.
- Round axis ticks to two or three significant digits and show exact values with units in tooltips.
- Title each chart with its takeaway, add a source and date line, and offer a data-table toggle.
- Avoid 3D charts, gradient fills, drop shadows on bars, heavy gridlines, pie charts above five slices and animations over 600ms.

title: Responsive and Mobile-First Layout
hint: Responsive layouts, mobile-first CSS, breakpoints and touch targets
text:
- Write base styles for 360-390px, then add min-width breakpoints at 640, 768, 1024 and 1280px.
- Use grid with repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 280px), 1fr)) for card sets and flex for toolbars; avoid fixed container widths.
- Guarantee no horizontal scroll at 320px: min-width: 0 on flex and grid children, overflow-wrap: anywhere, wide tables in an overflow container.
- Make touch targets at least 44x44 CSS px with 8px gaps, enlarging hit areas with padding rather than visuals.
- Replace hover-only interactions with tap or focus equivalents; never hide essential actions behind hover.
- Use clamp() for fluid type and spacing, e.g. clamp(2rem, 1.2rem + 3vw, 4.5rem), instead of jumps at breakpoints.
- Use dvh for full-height mobile sections and env(safe-area-inset-*) for fixed bars.

title: Motion and Micro-interactions
hint: Animations, transitions, hover and press feedback, entrance effects
text:
- Allow one signature motion moment per page plus feedback on controls; decorative looping animation is off by default.
- Animate only transform and opacity; never width, height, top, left, margin or box-shadow.
- Use 150-250ms for UI transitions and 300-450ms for entrances, with ease-out such as cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).
- Give every control press (scale 0.97), hover and focus-visible feedback within 100ms.
- Stagger reveals 60-90ms per item, rising 16-24px with opacity, triggered once on entry via IntersectionObserver.
- Keep content visible by default and add reveal classes from script so text survives if JavaScript fails.
- Wrap motion in prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, removing travel and keeping only opacity changes under 200ms.

title: Accessibility and WCAG 2.2
hint: Accessibility audits, WCAG contrast, keyboard focus and screen readers
text:
- Use semantic HTML first: button for actions, a for links, a label on every input, one h1, and main and nav landmarks; add ARIA only when needed.
- Keep body text at 4.5:1 and large text (18pt, or 14pt bold) at 3:1; focus rings and control boundaries need 3:1 against neighbours.
- Make every control keyboard-operable in DOM order with a visible focus ring of at least 2px; never remove outline without a replacement.
- Add a skip link first; move focus into dialogs on open, keep it there, and return it to the trigger on close.
- Give icon-only buttons an aria-label, give images alt text that states purpose, and hide decorative SVG with aria-hidden.
- Survive 200% text resize, 320px reflow and text-spacing overrides (1.5 line-height, 0.12em letter-spacing) without clipping.
- Announce async results with role=status and failed submissions with role=alert; never rely on colour alone.

title: Tailwind CSS v4 Practice
hint: Tailwind CSS styling, theme tokens, utility organisation and dark variant
text:
- Define tokens in an @theme block (--color-*, --font-*, --spacing-*, --radius-*) so bg-accent and font-display are generated from one source.
- Use :root for plain variables that must not create utilities; use @theme only when a value should map to a utility class.
- Keep the default 4px spacing unit and use p-4 or gap-6; promote any arbitrary value used twice, such as p-[13px], into @theme.
- Enable class dark mode with @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *)) and style with semantic colour tokens, not raw shades.
- Extract repeated class strings into components instead of @apply chains; reserve @apply for third-party markup.
- Write mobile-first: base utility first, then md: and lg: overrides; avoid max-* breakpoints as the default.
- Merge prop-driven classes with cn() built on clsx and tailwind-merge; never concatenate p-2 and p-4 into one string.

title: React UI Components (shadcn/Radix style)
hint: React UI components with shadcn/ui, Radix primitives and variants
text:
- Build dialogs, popovers, selects, tabs and menus on Radix or React Aria instead of hand-rolling focus management and ARIA state.
- Define variants with class-variance-authority using semantic names (default, destructive, outline, ghost) and one defaultVariants object.
- Forward refs, spread remaining props onto the root element, and merge className last through cn().
- Use asChild or Slot so a Button can render as a link without nesting interactive elements.
- Stay uncontrolled by default, with value and onValueChange for controlled use; do not copy props into useState.
- Keep components presentational; fetching and business logic live in hooks or the route layer.
- Style open, selected and disabled states with data-state and aria-* attributes, not boolean className branches.

title: HTML Email Templates
hint: HTML email layouts, newsletters and transactional templates
text:
- Build with nested tables using role="presentation", cellpadding 0, cellspacing 0 and border 0; flexbox and grid break in Outlook desktop.
- Set a 600px maximum width on a centred table with a fluid 100% wrapper for narrow screens.
- Inline critical CSS on each element, keep the style block for media queries and dark mode, and keep the message under 102KB to avoid Gmail clipping.
- Build CTA buttons as a padded table cell with background colour and an inline-block link, never background images.
- Give every image width, height, alt text and display: block, with a background colour behind it.
- Use Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif for body text; load web fonts only as progressive enhancement.
- Add 90-100 characters of hidden preheader text and keep visible copy under 200 words with one primary CTA.

title: SVG Icons and Logo Marks
hint: SVG icons, logo marks, inline vector graphics and icon sets
text:
- Draw icons on a 24x24 viewBox with 1.5-2px strokes and round caps and joins; leave width and height off the root so CSS sizes them.
- Use currentColor for fill and stroke so icons inherit text colour in both themes.
- Keep one icon style per product: one stroke width, one corner radius, all outline or all filled; never mix icon sets.
- Strip editor metadata, transforms and unused defs, and round coordinates to two decimals.
- Mark decorative SVG with aria-hidden="true" and focusable="false"; give meaningful SVG role="img" and a title.
- Reuse icons through an SVG symbol sprite referenced with use href instead of duplicating paths.
- Give logo marks clear space equal to the mark height, and test them at 16px and in single colour.

title: Presentation and Slide Visual Design
hint: Slide decks and presentations: hierarchy and one message per slide
text:
- Give every slide one message as a full-sentence headline of 12 words or fewer; the headline states the takeaway, not the topic.
- Use a 16:9 grid with 5-7% margins; body at 18pt minimum, headlines at 32-44pt, and at most six bullets of six words each.
- Put one visual per slide, a chart, diagram, photo or large number; never stack a chart, a table and bullets together.
- Limit the palette to background, text, one accent and one neutral, with at least 4.5:1 body-text contrast on the projected background.
- Keep one template with the same title position, margins and footer with page number and source.
- Move long explanations into speaker notes; avoid paragraphs, clip art and gradient or shadow decoration.
- End on one slide that states the ask or next step.

title: Three.js and WebGL Scenes
hint: Three.js, WebGL and canvas 3D scenes, rendering performance and loops
text:
- Create the renderer once with setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2)); handle resize with setSize, not per frame.
- Drive the loop with renderer.setAnimationLoop and a clock delta; never tie motion speed to frame count.
- Dispose geometries, materials, textures and the renderer on teardown, and remove the canvas and listeners, to avoid GPU leaks in SPAs.
- Reuse geometries and materials, switch to InstancedMesh beyond about 100 identical objects, and keep mobile draw calls under about 200.
- Pause rendering when the canvas is offscreen or the tab is hidden, and lower the pixel ratio on weak devices.
- Use MeshStandardMaterial with an environment map and at most three lights; load glTF with Draco or KTX2 compression.
- Stop auto-rotation under prefers-reduced-motion and give the canvas a static fallback image and a text description.

title: Forms, Validation and Microcopy
hint: Forms, validation errors, empty states, button labels and microcopy
text:
- Use one column with labels above fields; never use placeholder text as the label.
- Validate on blur for single fields and on submit for the form; show each error beside its field with the fix, e.g. 'Enter a date like 12/05/2026'.
- Write errors in plain words that state the problem and the fix; avoid 'Invalid input' and apologies.
- Name buttons by outcome ('Save changes', 'Delete project'); never bare 'Submit', 'OK' or 'Yes' for destructive actions.
- Write empty states as one sentence on what appears here plus one button to create the first item.
- Keep one term per object across the flow, sentence case, and no ALL CAPS or exclamation marks.
- Set type, inputmode and autocomplete attributes so mobile keyboards and autofill work; preserve input after errors.

title: Native Mobile App UI (iOS and Android)
hint: Native iOS or Android app screens and tab bars
text:
- Use a bottom tab bar with three to five labelled items for primary navigation; avoid hamburger menus for top-level sections.
- Keep touch targets at least 44x44 pt on iOS and 48x48 dp on Android, with 8pt or dp gaps.
- Place primary actions in the bottom thumb zone; use the large title on iOS and a 64dp top app bar on Android.
- Use system text styles so type scales with settings: body 17pt with Dynamic Type on iOS, sp units on Android.
- Keep content inside safe areas for the status bar and home indicator, with 16pt or 16dp side margins.
- Use native segmented controls, sheets, switches and pull-to-refresh before building custom widgets.
- Confirm destructive actions with a dialog or action sheet that names the consequence; avoid web-style hover states.
